recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: Enums, Models, and Shared Infrastructure
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency leaf modules first. leave-type (enum), leave-status (enum + transition rules), and the shared db connection / base repository are already in place. Add the audit module (model + repository + service) since it has no domain dependencies and is needed by everything else. Add the employee module (model + repository + service) — depends only on audit.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Policy & Balance Domain Services
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-policy depends only on leave-type (Phase 1). leave-balance depends on leave-type, leave-policy, employee, and audit (all Phase 1). Build repositories, service interfaces, and service implementations for both. These are the core domain logic modules that leave-request will orchestrate.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Notification Module
recommended_phases.rationale: notification depends only on employee (Phase 1). Build the notification model, repository, service interface, and service implementation. This is a supporting infrastructure module that leave-request will call after state changes.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Leave Request Orchestration & API Surface
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-request depends on everything above. Build the LeaveRequest model, repository, service interface, service implementation (orchestrates policy checks, balance validation/deduction, audit recording, and notifications), controller, route definitions, and input validation schemas. This is the largest phase — the service orchestrates all cross-module workflows.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries

- **Domain layer** (innermost): leave-type, leave-status — pure enums and value objects, zero dependencies
- **Domain services**: leave-policy, leave-balance, employee — models + repository interfaces + service interfaces + service implementations; depend only on domain layer and audit
- **Infrastructure**: audit, notification — cross-cutting; audit is a leaf with no domain deps; notification depends only on employee
- **Application orchestration** (outermost domain-facing): leave-request — orchestrates policy checks, balance validation/deduction, audit recording, and notification dispatch
- **Presentation**: leave-request controller + routes + validation schemas — Fastify route handlers, input validation (GP-003), RBAC enforcement (GP-005)

## Key design decisions

1. **leave-balance is a separate module** from leave-request because balance is an independent domain concept with its own lifecycle (accrual, fiscal-year rollover, manual adjustments). leave-request calls into it but does not own it.
2. **leave-policy is a separate module** because policies are configured by HR independently of any single leave request. leave-request queries policy for entitlement days, manager-approval flag, and minimum notice.
3. **Audit is a leaf module** — it has zero domain dependencies. Every state-changing service calls audit. This satisfies GP-002.
4. **Notification is a separate module** — it depends on employee (to resolve manager/recipient info) but nothing else. leave-request calls it after every state transition.
5. **employee module** exposes only what other modules need: getEmployeeById, getManagerId, isActive, getTeamMembers. It does NOT expose full CRUD — that stays internal.
6. **All repositories are behind interfaces** (GP-001). Services depend on repository interfaces, never on concrete repositories or the db connection directly.
7. **leave-request service is the sole orchestrator** — it is the only module that wires together policy + balance + audit + notification. No other module has this breadth of dependencies.

## Dependency direction verification

```
leave-request ──→ leave-balance ──→ leave-policy ──→ leave-type
    │                  │
    │                  └──→ employee ──→ audit
    │                  └──→ audit
    │
    ├──→ leave-status (leaf)
    ├──→ leave-type (leaf)
    ├──→ leave-policy ──→ leave-type
    ├──→ employee ──→ audit
    ├──→ audit (leaf)
    └──→ notification ──→ employee ──→ audit
```

All arrows point inward. No cycles.
